examples.problem:
Given that the points $A$ and $B$ with coordinates $(-2,4)$ and $(2,-4),$ respectively,  lie on a diameter of a circle centered at the origin, what is the equation of the circle?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13956996/assets/1909e28f4fa0376eb59fc1d1a117d10e9fbe4580aee1706e90516d84dede5940.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The equation of a circle with radius $r,$ centered at the origin, is 

$$
x^2 + y^2 = r^2.
$$

Now, we first calculate the diameter $AB\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{(-2-2)^{2}+{(4-(-4))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter, the radius is

$$
r=\dfrac{AB}{2} = \dfrac {4\sqrt{5}}{2}=2\sqrt5.
$$

So, the equation of the circle is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={(2\sqrt{5})}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Which equation describes the set of all points $(x,y)$ in the coordinate plane that are a distance of $12$ units from the origin?
feedback.worked_solution:
The set of all points $(x,y)$ that are a distance of $12$ units from the origin defines a circle with radius $r=12$ centered at the origin, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13956996/assets/ae57797a973213ad2b8050a937c449b83e8503c42d3fe5783ad23950a47c1046.png)

So, the required equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={12}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =144.\end{aligned}
$$
